title: 4 AWG compact-stranded aluminium XHHW-2 building wire

sources.citation: Typical published construction of 4 AWG aluminium XHHW-2 (a cable maker's public AA-8000 XHHW-2 datasheet, read; no ampacity column; listed to UL 44, cited by number): compact-stranded Class B AA-8000-series aluminium alloy, 7 strands, under a single cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) wall of 1.14 mm, made in black. Rated 90 °C wet or dry: the pinned insulation row xhhw2. Aluminium building wire starts at 12 AWG (NFPA 70-2023 Art. 310.3(A), by number). Paraphrased; no table copied.

AA-8000-series aluminium alloy (ASTM B800, cited by number, paywalled, not read) at an assumed minimum 61.0 % IACS: the pinned materials row aluminiumAa8000 (NBS Handbook 109). Not 'EC-grade'. The area comes from the AWG definition (AWG_GAUGES) for compact strands too.

A stranded conductor's resistance is its nominal area's times a lay factor of 1.02 for concentric Class B/C stranding up to 4/0 (NBS Handbook 100, Copper Wire Tables, 1966, its stranded-conductor tables and appendix; NBS Handbook 109, Aluminum Wire Tables, 1972, its twist factor of 1.02; both read in full in the P3 source pre-audit): the helical strands are longer than the conductor. Paraphrased; no table reproduced.
